items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: I used to love to see him come in in the morning with his drum strapped on his back.

ctx.x: Yes, we've, a lot of people have told us about him.
Oh, he was great. I used to love to see him come in in the morning with his drum strapped on his back. That's how they carried the drums.
Well, he did? I didn't notice. The bass drum? The bass drum on the back and snare drum in his hand. You know, some people tell us about one time he had a collapsible drum that folded up.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: I met them and I knew them. They knew me real well. I was just a kid.

ctx.x: I think he came from Memphis. But this guy was a trick drummer. Oh yeah. And of course you had old man Cottrell that was strictly a drummer. He was a Finnish musician drummer. Of course my daddy knew these people and he was real close friends with them. And he used to tell me. And I met them and I knew them. They knew me real well. I was just a kid. But the friendship always is beautiful.
What about the View of Korea in those days at Bourbon Street and all that? When did Bourbon Street start booming? Do you remember?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I mentioned Larry Cottrell's daddy yesterday at the concert.

ctx.x: Did you ever see him on a bicycle? Somebody was telling me he used to even ride a bicycle.

Well, if it was, it was in the days that he was playing here with Bunk Jones, not with Bunk, with what's the trumpet player, the first one? Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. Maybe in those days he might have been a younger man. He might have rode a bicycle then. You mean with that bass on his back? Yeah. Yes, I've heard him say that. I mentioned Larry Cottrell's daddy yesterday at the concert. I used to lug those drums all the way from his house up to Clay Hall Street. And then there was a whole set of drums on his…
Well, he had special drums, too, though, they said.
